summary:
Project Title: Space Memory (Digital Archive of Space Exploration)

Space Memory is an interactive educational platform designed to preserve and share the history of humanity’s exploration of space with future generations. The project brings together important space missions, scientific discoveries, and the stories of spacecraft that have explored or are still exploring the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Through the platform, users can discover space missions, explore mission locations using interactive maps, read informative stories, and reinforce their knowledge through interactive quizzes. Significant space exploration programs, including the Apollo missions, Mars exploration rovers, and Voyager probes, are featured as part of this digital archive.

The main goal of Space Memory is to make space science more understandable, accessible, and engaging for everyone. By preserving humanity’s scientific achievements in space in a digital environment, the project aims to inspire younger generations, encourage curiosity, and promote interest in science, technology, and space exploration.
details:
Space Memory is an interactive web-based educational platform that preserves and presents the history of human space exploration. It brings together selected missions to the Moon, Mars, and deep space in a single digital archive.

The platform includes 10 selected missions: Apollo 11, 15, 16, and 17; Mars Pathfinder–Sojourner; Spirit; Opportunity; Phoenix; Voyager 1; and Voyager 2. Users can search and filter missions, explore detailed mission profiles, navigate interactive Moon and Mars globes, save favorite missions, listen to Turkish narration, read educational stories, explore a space glossary, and test their knowledge through an eight-question quiz.

The project aims to make space science more accessible and engaging, especially for students and young learners. Its responsive web design allows users to explore the content on different devices.

The prototype uses web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with browser-based speech synthesis for narration. NASA mission information is used as a reference for the educational content. Future development may include more missions, expanded scientific data, additional languages, and improved accessibility.
